In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.Roll declined only Advantage (`p.Roll == D20Mode.Advantage`), rolling a Disadvantage roll as one d20; this test went red (the Disadvantage case).

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.Roll rolled a roll with both as one d20, as map 2.0.0's draws counts it (`p.Roll is not (D20Mode.Straight or D20Mode.AdvantageAndDisadvantage)`); this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; the InitiativeRoll handler defaulted a missing ScoreOption to `InitiativeScoreOptionStatement.Rolling("default")`; this test went red. It went red too when a missing IdenticalCreatures defaulted to `IdenticalCreaturesStatement.None("default")`.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; Ruleset.Identity named version 5; this test went red on the rendered identity and the pinned SHA-256, and no other did. Under map 2.0.0 it went red too when the map's assertedBy word for the players was not the engine's (`TieDecider.Players => "the players"`), when the map's assertedBy for initiative-ties was narrowed to ["GM"], and when the GM decided only all-monster ties. Under map 1.0.0 it went red under the dropped-modifier, reverse-draw-order and d19 mutations above, and under the ascending-order and tie-breaks-ignored mutations of initiative-order. The version mutation is re-run at every bump: under ruleset version 2 it was version 3, under version 3 (the movement and space batch) version 4, and under version 4 (the attacks batch) version 5; each time this test went red on the rendered identity and the pinned SHA-256, and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.Order ranked lowest first (`.OrderBy(c => c.Initiative)`); this test went red. It went red too when TurnOrder.TurnsInRound reversed the order in even rounds, and when a tie break was demanded where there was no tie (`assignments.IsEmpty && assignments.Length > 99`).

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.Order ignored the stated tie breaks, keeping tied combatants in listing order (`.ThenBy(c => 0)`); this test went red, and so did the seeded replay. It went red too under the ascending-order mutation.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.BreakTies caught AssertionRequiredException and inferred each tie's order as listed, attributed to "inferred"; this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.BreakTies read the assertion even with no tie (`assignments.IsEmpty && assignments.Length > 99`); this test went red. It went red too when a tie between a monster and a player character was assigned to the players.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run, under map 2.0.0; InitiativeRules dropped the check of the stated party against the map's assertedBy party for the tie (`if (false && statedParty != TieDeciders.AssertedBy(tie.Decider))`); this test went red and no other did. Under map 1.0.0 (the check then `tieBreak.DecidedBy != tie.Decider`) it went red the same way (the two wrong-decider cases), when a tie break ordering more than the tied set was accepted (`IsSupersetOf` for `SetEquals`), and, after the "no tie exists" case was added (it had stayed green without it), when tie breaks for no tie were accepted (`remaining.Count > 99`).

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; TieDeciders.Named skipped the map's assertedBy and matched the engine's own deciders (`if (false && !MapEntries.InitiativeTies.AssertedBy.Contains(party, ...))`); this test went red and no other did. It went red too when the engine's word for the players was not the map's (`TieDecider.Players => "the players"`), and when the generated MapEntries.InitiativeTies.AssertedBy was narrowed to ["GM"] (so did every test with a players' tie, and the seeded replay).

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run, under map 2.0.0; InitiativeRules.Assign named the GM only for all-monster ties (`TieDeciders.Named(tie.All(c => c.Kind == CombatantKind.Monster) ? "GM" : "players")`), so a monster tied with a player character went to the players; this test went red, and so did the seeded replay. It had gone red under the same mutation under map 1.0.0.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.Assign assigned a monster tied with a non-player character to the GM (`if (false && monster && nonPlayerCharacter)`); this test went red. It went red too when the decline's Attempted named initiative-ties instead of initiative-ties-uncovered (both entries cite the same page, so only Attempted tells them apart), and when the decline cited initiative-score-option's locator.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules resolved a tie the players stated they did not agree on, ordering it as listed (`if (false && tieBreak.PlayersDidNotAgree)`); this test went red and no other did. Re-run under map 2.0.0: red again, and no other test.
